q: Is the study identified as developing, validating or updating a prediction model (regression or ML)?
hint: Title/abstract should state model type, target population and outcome.

q: Are data sources, eligibility, recruitment and setting clearly described?
hint: Cohort, registry, EHR, dates, centres, inclusion/exclusion.

q: Are participant characteristics and sample size justified?
hint: Flow of participants, events per predictor, sample-size rationale.

q: Is the outcome defined, measured and timed without knowledge of predictors?
hint: Outcome definition, blinding of assessment, prediction horizon.

q: Are predictors defined, measured and timed clearly, including preprocessing?
hint: Definitions, measurement methods, handling at prediction time.

q: Is missing data reported and handled appropriately?
hint: Amount missing per predictor/outcome, imputation method, complete-case justification.

q: Is the modelling approach fully specified (algorithm, tuning, validation split)?
hint: Algorithm, hyperparameters, tuning, train/validation/test split, leakage safeguards.

q: Was data leakage ruled out (patient/site/time separation)?
hint: Same patient, scanner or site in train and test inflates performance.

q: Are discrimination, calibration and clinical utility reported with uncertainty?
hint: AUC plus calibration plot/slope, decision curve, CIs — not point estimates alone.

q: Are subgroup and fairness analyses reported?
hint: Performance by sex, age, site, ethnicity; error analysis.

q: Was the model evaluated on an independent (external) cohort?
hint: Temporal, geographic or fully independent validation; differences discussed.

q: Are data, code and model details shared enough to reproduce?
hint: Access terms, preprocessing, seeds, versions, model card.

q: Do claims and intended use match what was actually tested?
hint: No leap from retrospective AUC to bedside benefit; limitations and harms stated.
